div.head: II As 24.1
div.ab: ⁊ ðæt nan cyping ne sy Sunnondagum; gif hit ðonne hwa dó, þolige ðæs ceapes ⁊ gesylle XXX scll' (to wite).
And þæt nán ceaping ne sy Sunnandagum; gif hit hwa dó, ðolige ðæs ceapgyld ⁊ sylle XXX scill.

Et non sint mercata aliqua (fiat aliqua negotiatio uel forensis actio) die dominica. Si quis hoc faciat (presumat), perdat suum ceapgildum (ipsum captale) et soluat XXX sol. (emendet ouerhyrnessam meam).
⁊ ðæt nan cyping ne sy Sunnondagum; gif hit ðonne hwa dó, þolige ðæs ceapes ⁊ gesylle XXX scll' to wite.
Und dass kein Kaufen an Sonntagen geschehe; wenn das aber jemand thut, verliere er das Kaufgut und zahle 30 Schill. (zur Strafe H).
And that no buying take place on Sundays; but if anyone does that, let him lose the goods bought and pay 30 shillings (as a fine, H).
And no trading shall take place on Sundays; and if anyone does so he shall lose the goods and pay a fine of 30 shillings.

note.quote: the clause ('24:1') banning Sunday trading, its absence logically connected with the deliberations at Thunderfield ('IV') that abrogated previous decisions about Sunday business

note.label: revises (lifts ban)
note.quote: Within a few more years, however, the king seems to have changed his mind. The ban on Sunday commerce was apparently lifted.

H’s ceapes ist laut EGu archetyp; und vielleicht daraus captale Q ii; ceapgild in lq heisst ‘Ersatzgeld’
H’s ceapes is shown by EGu to be the reading of the archetype; and captale Q ii perhaps derives from it; ceapgild in lq means ‘compensation money’
Q i hat originales kleinstes Strafgeldfixum; s. d. Gl 6 a. Der klerikale Verf. bedrohte später Sonntagshandel mit 120 Schill. (vgl. Gl Sonntag 6), was beispiellos hoch
Q i has the original, smallest fixed fine; see that word in Gl 6 a. The clerical author later threatened Sunday trading with 120 shill. (cf. Gl Sonntag 6), which is unprecedentedly high
